rounds.text: QMS Medical Allied Services demonstrates superior operational efficiency with a ROCE of 12.91%, which outperforms the sector benchmark of 11.77% [E10]. This efficiency is backed by exceptional cash generation, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of 1.58x and free cash flow of Rs 19 Cr as of March 2026 [E24, E26]. Despite its strong performance, the company trades at an EV/EBITDA of 14.25x, which represents a discount to the sector benchmark of 15.95x [E11]. Recent performance highlights robust momentum with year-over-year sales growth of 22% and net profit growth of 25% [E54, E56]. Market appreciation is building, as shown by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and a 12-month price return of 84.0% [E41, E42]. Conceded: the company has seen a -15% decline in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15], and the promoter holding has decreased by 5.56 percentage points since December 2022 [E31, E52]. The company maintains a disciplined capital return policy, characterized by a healthy dividend payout of 56.4% [E49].

The core risk facing QMS Medical Allied Services Ltd lies in a distinct divergence between market pricing and fundamental delivery, evidenced by a price-led signal where recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 88% [E47]. This premium valuation is not supported by current financial reality, given that a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 153 against a market price of Rs 177, leaving a negative margin of safety of -15.9% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands a 12.0% earnings growth rate, which outpaces the 10.0% assumed in the base case [E37]. Fundamental headwinds compound these valuation strains, marked by a compounded profit growth of -15% over the trailing twelve months [E15] and a low 3-year median return on equity of 12% [E51]. Insider behavior aligns with these pressures, as promoter holdings have dropped by 5.56 percentage points from 73.67% in Dec 2022 to 68.11% in Sep 2026 [E31], alongside a reduction in foreign institutional ownership [E32]. Finally, investors must contend with severe historical volatility of 62.0% [E44] and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -68.5% [E43]. Conceded: the company maintains a healthy dividend payout of 56.4% [E49] and demonstrates strong cash conversion of 1.58x where profits are fully backed by operating cash flow [E24].

While the bear highlights a negative margin of safety from a discounted cash flow model [E36], the 12.0% earnings growth required to justify the current price [E37] is actually conservative when compared to the company's recent delivery of 22% sales growth [E54] and 25% net profit growth [E56, E57]. Although trailing twelve-month profit growth was negative [E15], the company’s EV/EBITDA of 14.25x remains more attractive than the sector benchmark of 15.95x [E11], and its ROCE of 12.91% outperforms both the sector benchmark of 11.77% [E10] and the sector median of 12.5% [E62]. Conceded: promoter and foreign institutional holdings have decreased [E31, E32], yet this is countered by domestic institutions entering the stock with a 1.30 percentage point increase [E33], resulting in an overall positive institutional money flow [E34]. The bear's concerns over historical volatility [E44] are offset by a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E41] and a price trend that remains robustly above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40]. Finally, the company's strong cash conversion of 1.58x [E24] and its high rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 [E53] suggest that the market is beginning to recognize fundamental improvements that the bear's lagging indicators overlook.

However, the bull's reliance on recent sales and profit spikes [E54, E56] ignores the reality that compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months stands firmly at -15% [E15]. Furthermore, pointing to a reverse DCF requirement of 12.0% earnings growth [E37] dismisses the core risk flagged by the DCF model: a negative margin of safety of -15.9% at the current price of Rs 177 [E35, E36]. While the bull celebrates positive institutional money flow [E34], it glosses over the steady multi-year dilution of promoter ownership from 73.67% down to 68.11% [E31]. The claim that technical strength [E40, E41] offsets volatility [E44] ignores the historical record of a -68.5% peak-to-trough drawdown [E43] and the warning that price growth has outpaced profit growth by 88% [E47]. Finally, rising borrowings of Rs 74 Cr against Rs 60 Cr previously [E29] reveal that leverage pressures are building beneath the surface despite strong single-year cash conversion [E24].

Conceded: [E15]. While compounded trailing profit growth is negative [E15], the rules-based screen scores the company 86 out of 100 with a BUY rating driven by robust year-over-year sales and profit surges [E53, E54, E56]. Dismissing the valuation via DCF ignores that the company generated robust operating and free cash flow of Rs 19 Cr in March 2026, fully backing its reported profits with a 1.58x cash conversion ratio [E24, E25, E26]. Although promoter holding declined over multiple years [E31], domestic institutions have increased their stake [E33], and recent institutional money flow reads positive [E34]. Technical strength with a relative-strength rating of 100 and prices holding above both moving averages are backed by a strong 84.0% twelve-month price return rather than arbitrary optimism [E40, E41, E42]. Finally, the rise in borrowings [E29] occurs alongside a healthy dividend payout of 56.4% [E49] and an ROCE of 12.91%, which outpaces the sector benchmark of 11.77% [E10].

Conceded: [E10]. While the rules-based screen scores the company 86 out of 100 [E53], that mechanical output conflicts directly with the trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of -15% [E15]. The reliance on robust cash flow of Rs 19 Cr [E25] and a 1.58x cash conversion ratio [E24] overlooks the reality that borrowings expanded from Rs 60 Cr to Rs 74 Cr [E29] while the intrinsic value derived from a discounted cash flow sits below the market price at Rs 153, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -15.9% [E35, E36]. Conceded: [E33]. Pointing to increased domestic institutional stakes [E33] ignores the broader structural distribution trend where promoters dropped their holdings by 5.56 percentage points and foreign institutions also reduced exposure [E31, E32]. Technical strength and a relative-strength rating of 100 [E41] merely mask the underlying valuation stretch, as a reverse DCF exposes that the current price already prices in 12.0% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 10.0% [E37], validating the engine's warning that price growth exceeds profit growth by 88% and expectations are running ahead of delivery [E47].
